transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-14
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Jordan Reyes (CTO, Northbridge), Maya Patel (Head of Ops), Tyler Shaw (Procurement), Sofia Kim (SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick check on renewal; exploring upgrade to dedicated capacity, add us-west region for lower latency on west coast hubs, discuss committed usage and contract extension, run benchmarks to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood, i think we got everyone? Jordan, Maya, Tyler, Sofia, hi thanks for making time.
[00:18] Jordan Reyes: Yep here, sorry slight delay on my end. Lots going on this morning.
[00:26] Maya Patel: Morning, Maya here. ready to talk renewal and expansion.
[00:34] Alex Chen: Great, quick agenda - status of current usage, proposed dedicated upgrade, adding us-west region, pricing implications, and next steps - any additions?
[00:45] Tyler Shaw: Procurement is mainly timing and PO questions, nothing technical.
[00:51] Priya Singh: I'll dig into the benchmark plan and what we'll measure.
[00:57] Jordan Reyes: Sounds good. We've been hitting some tail latency during peak shipments on the west coast so region is a priority.
[01:12] Sofia Kim: yeah we've seen 120-160 ms token latency spikes in those windows vs 40-60 ms east coast.
[01:24] Alex Chen: Thanks, that aligns with what we saw in the dashboards. Briefly on current contract - you're on hosted with burst credits, correct?
[01:34] Maya Patel: yes hosted API, some caching but mostly direct calls, and the renewal comes up in July.
[01:41] Alex Chen: Ok. Two primary options: 1) Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput, better isolation), or 2) keep hosted and add regional routing + cache tuning. Dedicated gives you guaranteed p99s.
[01:56] Jordan Reyes: What kind of uplift in cost are we talking for dedicated? ballpark.
[02:04] Alex Chen: rough ballpark - for your typical throughput we'd estimate committed tier pricing about 1.8x current hosted baseline but per-token unit cost drops for steady traffic; plus reduced tail latency. We'll send detailed pricing.
[02:21] Tyler Shaw: that 1.8x is big, need to see committed discounts, and multi-year option.
[02:29] Alex Chen: absolutely, multi-year (24 months) and higher commits move the multiplier toward parity - we'll model a few scenarios.
[02:37] Priya Singh: From SE side, dedicated also lets us optimize batching and local KV cache per pool which can reduce effective cost per token by 20-30% depending on cache hit rates, so the headline cost isn't the whole picture.
[02:55] Maya Patel: good point, we need the business case with real numbers.
[03:01] Jordan Reyes: Also curious about adding a us-west region - what's the deployment lift?
[03:07] Priya Singh: we can bring up a secondary pool in us-west, it's straightforward - configuration + infra takes a day for provisioning, then model warm-up, maybe 24-48 hours to reach steady-state. Data residency isn't an issue since it's still US. Traffic steering can be regional or geography-based.
[03:27] Sofia Kim: Do we get replicated KV caches or separate per-region?
[03:31] Priya Singh: separate per-region caches, we can add cross-region pre-warm if you want stronger warm starts. There's a small consistency window if you write session-level data.
[03:44] Tyler Shaw: For procurement we also need the SLA language - any changes with dedicated?
[03:50] Alex Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime guarantees at the contract level, and 24/7 priority support. We'll include SLA addendum in the renewal paperwork.
[04:02] Jordan Reyes: On security: KMS and audit logs are must-haves. We saw a note about Private offering - is that required for us?
[04:12] Alex Chen: You don't need Private unless you require VPC-only control plane or on-prem air-gapped. Our dedicated pools support customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 controls while staying in Redwood hosted control plane.
[04:27] Maya Patel: Good. Back to cost: can you run a head-to-head benchmark so we can present to finance?
[04:36] Priya Singh: Yes - propose a 72-hour benchmark with dedicated pool in us-east + us-west, using your peak traces. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tail tokens, and cost per 1M tokens.
[04:49] Jordan Reyes: That works. We'll provide traffic samples and the peak windows.
[04:54] Sofia Kim: I'll extract the heatmap and traffic windows by tomorrow.
[04:59] Priya Singh: perfect. We'll instrument detailed tracing so you can see token-level breakdowns - network, decode, kernel time etc.
[05:10] Alex Chen: Next, on contract length - finance likes committed usage discounts. If you commit to 12 months vs 24 months any preference?
[05:19] Tyler Shaw: Prefer 12 months but open to 24 if the numbers are right. Need to see net present value.
[05:26] Alex Chen: We'll provide both scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[05:30] Jordan Reyes: Quick question - fallback behavior if us-west is down? we need graceful degradation to avoid order processing outages.
[05:38] Priya Singh: We'll configure smart routing with automatic fallback to us-east or to a lower-cost model variant; can set routing policy by latency or region. Canary & automatic fallback included.
[05:51] Maya Patel: Do we need to rework our client code for routing?
[05:55] Priya Singh: minimal - mostly you point to the same API but include region hint or let our routing handle it. We can share SDK snippets.
[06:05] Jordan Reyes: Ok. Any compliance docs we should review before contract sign?
[06:10] Alex Chen: We'll share SOC2, ISO27001 summary, KMS integration guide, and our private deployment whitepaper in the follow-up email.
[06:20] Tyler Shaw: please also include sample contract language for data retention and log access.
[06:24] Alex Chen: will do.
[06:28] Priya Singh: technical note - if you plan to use quantized model variants for cost, there may be minor quality delta. We'll include evals against your prompts as part of the benchmark.
[06:41] Jordan Reyes: That's important - we can't have regressions in customer-facing flows.
[06:45] Priya Singh: we'll include A/B tests and a few regression thresholds; if quality dips beyond threshold fallback to full-precision model.
[06:56] Maya Patel: timeline - renewal is mid-July, what's realistic to finish benchmark and have pricing finalized?
[07:02] Alex Chen: if benchmark starts next week and runs 72 hours, with 2 business days for analysis, we can have numbers by 2027-06-23. Pricing send by 2027-06-16 as discussed. Legal review may take 2-3 weeks.
[07:16] Tyler Shaw: procurement will need at least 10 business days to process a PO after finance signs off.
[07:23] Alex Chen: noted.
[07:26] Jordan Reyes: can we also get an estimate of cost impact if we enable prefix caching aggressively?
[07:33] Priya Singh: depends on hit rates. If you have high repetition in prompts (like templated shipping requests), you could see 25-35% token cost reduction. We'll include a simulation based on your trace.
[07:47] Sofia Kim: one more technical: how do model rollouts work in Dedicated? we want canary for new model versions.
[07:53] Priya Singh: same as hosted - canary, A/B, automatic fallback. In Dedicated you can pin a pool to a version and stage canary in a separate pool to measure before full switch.
[08:05] Maya Patel: great.
[08:08] Alex Chen: quick objection we sometimes hear - folks worry about vendor lock if committing long-term. Thoughts?
[08:15] Jordan Reyes: it's a concern, but if costs and performance are predictable it's acceptable. We just need exit clauses and data portability language.
[08:24] Alex Chen: we can add data export and portability terms; we'll include that in the renewal paperwork.
[08:31] Tyler Shaw: about the discount tiers, can you model a stepped commit where we start with smaller reserve in Q3 and scale up in Q4?
[08:39] Alex Chen: yes we can do staged commit with phased billing and a burst allowance. We'll show an example amortized model.
[08:49] Priya Singh: for benchmarking we'll include both steady-state and ramp tests to validate autoscale and burst behavior.
[08:58] Jordan Reyes: perfect.
[09:00] Alex Chen: ok let's capture next steps - Priya runs bench, Sofia sends heatmap, Alex sends pricing and SLA docs, Tyler confirms procurement timelines. Anything else?
[09:12] Maya Patel: can we get a short 20-30 minute tech walkthrough for our infra team while the benchmark runs?
[09:18] Priya Singh: yes we can schedule that; maybe day 2 of the benchmark so we have live metrics.
[09:24] Tyler Shaw: procurement prefers email confirmations for any pricing numbers.
[09:29] Alex Chen: will send formal email.
[09:33] Jordan Reyes: any blockers on our side? I don't think so.
[09:37] Maya Patel: none.
[09:40] Alex Chen: ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the benchmark plan and pricing sheet.
[09:47] Tyler Shaw: thanks, appreciate it.
[09:49] Priya Singh: thanks all.
[59:02] Meeting ended

Notes: transcript includes some slight ASR mistakes and swapped proper nouns; action items and next steps captured above. Links shared during call: "Renewal pricing template (link)"; "Dedicated pool whitepaper (link)"; "KMS integration guide (link)"
